description: The bar chart, titled "RoBERTa Size," compares the GLUE performance of different fine-tuning methods across two model sizes: "base" (blue bars) and "large" (orange bars), with the performance values shown on the vertical axis ranging from approximately 85.5 to 90. The horizontal axis lists seven fine-tuning methods: Prefix, Adaptor, LoRA, BitFit, S1-model, S4-model, and S5-model. For each method, two bars are displayed side-by-side, representing the performance of the base and large models. The "large" model consistently outperforms the "base" model across all methods, with the highest performance observed for the "S5-model" large configuration, which reaches a GLUE score of approximately 90. The "LoRA" method shows the second-highest performance for the large model, at about 89.7. In contrast, the "Adaptor" method shows the lowest performance for the base model, at approximately 85.8, and the "BitFit" method has a similarly low performance for the base model, around 85.5. The performance of the "base" model is relatively low for all methods, generally ranging from about 85.5 to 87.0, while the "large" model's performance is higher, ranging from about 85.6 to 90. The chart clearly illustrates that the "large" model size significantly enhances performance for all tested fine-tuning methods.
